items.content: With smartphone sales tanking by around 20 percent compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company laid out its plans to make a splash in the AI data center business, through partnerships with companies like Amazon and Meta announced earlier this year. The company expects that portion of its business to grow quickly, forecasting around $650 million in data center revenue during the first quarter of 2027. But it anticipates that will reach $5 billion by the end of 2027 and $15 billion by 2029.Considering the company’s total revenue for 2026 was $10.4 billion, that would constitute a significant share of its earnings. It confirmed during the call that it expects data centers to eventually account for around 30 percent of its business.That’s not quite as ambitious as AMD, which says that it expects over 80 percent of its revenue will eventually come from data centers. But it suggests there’s plenty of demand that needs to be filled and enough AI money to go around.RelatedAMD rides data center riches to ‘largest and most profitable’ quarter in historyIntel says it’s selling every affordable laptop chip it can makeData centers lost the midterms

items.titleZh: 智能手机销量下滑，高通大举押注数据中心
items.descriptionZh:
高通在2026财年第四季度财报电话会上明确表示，面对智能手机销售较2025年下滑约20%的压力，公司将把AI数据中心作为新的增长引擎。公司此前已宣布与亚马逊、Meta等超大规模云厂商合作，计划借此切入AI数据中心市场。高通预计，2027年第一季度数据中心业务收入约为6.5亿美元，到2027年底达到50亿美元，到2029年进一步增至150亿美元。作为参照，公司2026年总营收为104亿美元，因此数据中心业务若达到上述目标，将显著改变其收入结构。高通还确认，预计数据中心最终将占公司业务的约30%。

从技术层面看，这篇报道并未披露高通数据中心芯片的具体微架构、制程、内存带宽、互联规格或加速器型号，因此无法展开具体性能参数。可确认的是，其切入方式更偏向与亚马逊、Meta等云厂商合作，面向AI训练和推理所需的高能效计算与定制化加速需求。AI数据中心的核心技术挑战包括高算力密度、能效比、内存与互连带宽、规模化部署和软件生态；高通若能把其在低功耗计算和连接领域的积累延伸到数据中心场景，并通过定制合作锁定超大规模客户需求，将构成其业务创新的关键。但具体产品竞争力和技术细节仍有待后续披露。

从收入预测看，高通的数据中心业务呈现“低基数、高增速”特征：2027年第一季度约6.5亿美元，到2027年底50亿美元，意味着一年内大幅扩张；到2029年150亿美元，约为2027年第一季度规模的23倍。若以2026年104亿美元总营收为参照，150亿美元已超过该年总营收，因此30%占比目标隐含公司总营收同步增长或数据中心收入预测非常激进。与AMD预计未来80%以上收入来自数据中心相比，高通的30%目标相对温和，但也说明AI数据中心需求足够大、市场资金充足，竞争者仍有空间。

技术影响和应用场景方面，高通此举旨在降低对智能手机周期的依赖，形成第二增长曲线。AI数据中心业务可服务于大模型训练与推理、生成式AI服务、推荐系统、云计算和企业AI工作负载，并与亚马逊、Meta等云厂商的定制需求结合。若合作顺利落地，高通将从移动芯片供应商转向“移动+数据中心”双轮驱动；但执行风险包括合作规模能否兑现、产品能否在英伟达和AMD主导的数据中心加速市场中形成差异化，以及客户集中度和收入预测的可实现性。总体看，这是高通在手机业务承压下向AI基础设施转型的重要信号，但具体技术成色仍需产品与订单验证。

items.content: One of the basic problems of spending too much time on social media is that you are cooking your brain by reading posts from a pack of attention-seeking lunatics. If your social media of choice is the site formerly known as Twitter, and it is your main source of contact with the outside world, you may delusionally throw away nearly $500 million dollars on midterm elections, just like Elon Musk.In particular, $47 million of that money from Musk’s America PAC was aimed at defeating Texas Democrat James Talarico, who trounced Musk’s preferred Senate candidate, Ken Paxton, with 55 percent of the vote. Talarico even made Musk’s influence a central part of his campaign ads, with the slogan “Texas is not for sale.”The opposition to data centers is a way of making concrete how pissed off most people are with the tech industryHow did Musk get this so wrong? I blame the bubble of X. My former colleague Casey Newton, who has (with some well-earned shame) slunk back to X, explained that he did so because it was the site that was most influential with the AI crowd. In some sense, this is exactly the problem. The agentmaxxing loons of AI influencing are wildly out of touch with normal people. There is, right now, one very important bipartisan position in the United States, and it is: Fuck a data center.It’s pretty obvious that the opposition to data centers is a way of making concrete how pissed off most people are with the tech industry, particularly with the gangster tech regulation of late and the constant stream of threats coming from AI companies. These guys have really tied themselves and their AI aspirations to Donald Trump’s sinking ship, and if you’re hanging out on X all the time, that’s impossible to see, not least because the site’s owner, Musk, is shaping the algorithm in ways that make him feel good.Since Musk seems to have forgotten what it is like to experience joy, or even mild satisfaction, I have taken the liberty to make a list of things he could have bought to get him a better return on his investment. He probably could flip several things on this list for more money, but at minimum he could have gotten a little rush of pleasure from a new purchase:Larry Ellison’s private island ($300 million in 2012, $440 million in today’s dollars per CPI calculator) (source)13 Rolls-Royce La Rose Noire Droptails ($32 million) (source)5 The Graff Diamonds Hallucination watches ($55 million, $78 million today) (source)The Washington Post ($250 million in 2013, $360 million today) (source)30 Sunseeker 100 yachts (base price $14.6 million) (source)43 Hope diamonds ($300,000 in 1911, about $10.3 million today) (source)Ken Griffin’s NYC penthouse ($239.96 million in 2019, $321 million today) (source)76 New Zealand golden visas ($10 million plus $27,000 application fee in NZD, about $5.77 million in USD) (source)44 30-second Super Bowl commercials ($10 million) (source)At least 977 rides on Blue Origin’s New Shepard ($450,000) (source)Willem de Kooning’s Interchange (~$300 million, ~$400 million today) (source)$14.67 gift card to every Texan (~30 million Texans) (source)34 renovations of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool ($13.1 million) (source)223,000 Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards (at MSRP of $1,999) (source); 60,000 Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards (at “globalized normal price” of $7,240) (source)8 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show Fantasy Bras (source)His very own non-Grok version of The Odyssey (budget $250 million) (source)4 sets of Wachtell, Lipton lawyers from the Twitter takeover suit ($90 million fee) (source)But hey, at least changing the name of SpaceX’s “Superintelligence” division back to “Artificial Intelligence” is free!Musk spent last night deleting tweets so he wouldn’t look as stupid as he is. Too bad it’s not as easy to delete other things! Texans were already asking questions about sweetheart deals to benefit Musk, and now there’s a wave of politicians who ran against his money coming into power, including the governor and the attorney general of Texas. That may mean unredacting Gov. Greg Abbott’s Musk emails, for instance — answering some questions about the influence Musk bought with Texas Republicans.So actually, maybe the best investment on that list would be the dream team of lawyers who clobbered Musk on the Twitter deal — because Musk has a bunch of new enemies in power, and the simplest thing in the world they can do to curry favor with their voters is investigate him. Bet you’d never know that if you spent all your time on X.

items.titleZh: 埃隆·马斯克本可浪费4.46亿美元的17个更好办法
items.descriptionZh:
埃隆·马斯克在中期选举中投入近5亿美元政治资金，试图影响多场选战，但结果令人失望。其中4700万美元通过其美国政治行动委员会用于阻击得克萨斯州民主党人詹姆斯·塔拉里科，然而塔拉里科以55%的得票率击败了马斯克支持的参议院候选人肯·帕克斯顿，甚至在竞选广告中以“得州非卖品”为口号，将马斯克的影响力作为核心议题加以抨击。

文章认为，马斯克此次政治判断失误的根源在于沉迷于X平台所营造的信息回音室。作者引述前同事凯西·牛顿的观察指出，X在人工智能从业者群体中最具影响力，而AI圈中热衷于“智能体最大化”的狂热者与普通民众严重脱节。当前美国存在一个罕见的跨党派共识：对数据中心说“不”。这种反对本质上是公众对科技行业不满情绪的具体化表达，尤其是针对近期科技监管中的强势作风以及AI公司不断发出的威胁性言论。文章指出，科技从业者已将自身AI抱负与特朗普的政治命运捆绑，但如果整日泡在X上，就完全看不到这一现实，因为平台所有者马斯克正通过算法塑造让自己感觉良好的信息环境。

为讽刺马斯克的投资回报，文章列举了他本可以用这笔钱购买的其他项目，包括甲骨文创始人拉里·埃里森曾拥有的私人岛屿、13辆劳斯莱斯定制车型、5块格拉夫钻石幻觉腕表、《华盛顿邮报》、30艘Sunseeker 100游艇、43颗希望钻石、肯·格里芬的纽约顶层公寓、76份新西兰黄金签证、44条30秒超级碗广告、至少977次蓝色起源新谢泼德号太空旅行、德库宁的画作《交换》、给每位得州人发放14.67美元礼品卡、34次林肯纪念堂倒影池翻修、22.3万张英伟达RTX 5090显卡，或者4套曾用于推特收购诉讼的Wachtell律所律师团队。

文章最后指出，马斯克已开始删除推文以掩饰尴尬，但得州选民早已对有利于他的特殊交易提出质疑。随着包括州长和总检察长在内的多位曾与马斯克资金对抗的政治人物上台，马斯克用金钱在得州共和党人中换取的影响力可能面临调查，例如要求公开州长格雷格·阿博特与马斯克的往来邮件。文章讽刺道，或许清单上最值得的投资，恰恰是那支在推特收购案中击溃马斯克的律师团队，因为马斯克如今在权力层中树敌众多，而新上台的政客讨好选民最简单的方式，就是对他展开调查。

items.title: Nintendo ROM chip supplier Macronix quits to focus on chips for AI data centers, reports indicate
items.description: Macronix, one of Nintendo's ROM chip manufacturers, is shutting down the business to reallocate manufacturing for NOR and NAND flash chips that the AI industry demands.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 10 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The death of physical games could be getting closer as Macronix, one of Nintendo’s key ROM chip suppliers for Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges, is reportedly shutting down its ROM business to focus on manufacturing NOR and NAND flash chips to supply data centers, multiple reports claim. Storage is already becoming expensive, and Macronix’s move may force Nintendo to increase cartridge prices, produce more Game-Key cards, or lean more towards digital purchases.Go deeper with TH Premium: Memory (Image credit: SK Hynix)AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supplySamsung debuts three next-generation memory technologies for AI data centersThe future of DRAM: From DDR5 to future ICsHigh-bandwidth memory roadmapInside the history of DRAM price-fixing lawsuits"Nintendo's main memory chip maker is quitting the Switch business," MST Financial David Gibson reports on X. "Macronix, which makes the ROM chips in Switch 1 and Switch 2 game memory cards, is phasing out that business. There will be no new ROM products, and Q3 is the last quarter it reports ROM sales separately.1/4 Nintendo's main memory chip maker is quitting the Switch business Macronix, which makes the ROM chips in Switch 1 and Switch 2 game memory cards, is phasing out that business. There will be no new ROM products, and Q3 is the last quarter it reports ROM sales separately.November 4, 2026He notes that Macronix ROM sales in Q3 of this year dropped to 5%, compared to last year’s 26%. Furthermore, Gibson says that the NT$37.8 billion capital expenditure is allocated to NOR and NAND Flash, leaving none for ROM as the company shifts its manufacturing capacity to supply AI needs — Taipei Times corroborated the report, stating, "At the same time, Macronix is gradually phasing out of ROM production, Wu said. It also reports that Macronix’s capital expenditure is split into two phases, the NT$ 22 billion for expanding manufacturing capacity, followed by an additional NT$15.8 billion for NAND flash used in eMMCs and 3D NAND.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Gibson expects that Nintendo’s digital margins will grow through more Game-Key Cards or digital-only sales, but as Macronix isn’t the only source of ROM chips, “physical cards will likely carry on for some time.” Gibson further reports that digital margins have been slowly rising, with numbers fluctuating depending on the quarter due to major physical game launches.3/4 My view: Macronix isn't Nintendo's only game memory card maker, so physical cards will likely carry on for some time. But at the margin, digital will grow, through more Game-Key Cards (which hold a download key, not the game) and digital-only sales.November 4, 2026ROHM group companies ROHM Semiconductor and LAPIS Semiconductor still supply ROM chips to Nintendo, so it’s unlikely that Nintendo will eventually go digital-only in the near future like Sony and Microsoft’s recent plans. With one less supplier, however, Nintendo may be forced to increase prices on physical games. You may like Nintendo stands by physical games as Sony embraces a digital-only future NOR Flash and SLC NAND production are under threat as capacity gets routed to more profitable products — 'severe undersupply' threatens everyday electronics Micron discontinues 2GB GDDR7 chips for gaming GPUs as it pivots toward higher-density memory for AI The biggest loser in all of this (besides the gamers), however, may be fabless chip design company MegaChips. Nintendo doesn’t buy ROM chips from Macronix directly; MegaChips designs the ROM chips according to Nintendo’s needs and, having no manufacturing capacity, outsources it to Macronix. MegaChips’ 2022 company report states that Nintendo accounted for 87.8% of its sales, while Macronix accounted for 67.8% of its outsourced manufacturing purchases. The report even states that if Macronix could manufacture ROM chips, “MegaChips’ operating results may be impacted.” The 2022 document further says that there was no sign that the risk would become apparent; however, the risk just became very real, and we’re not aware of MegaChips’ contingency plan to deal with this situation. However, Macronix and MegaChips have likely talked amongst themselves about Macronix’s plans to stop ROM chip manufacturing, and have given MegaChips some time to find another manufacturer before Macronix shuts down the ROM chip business. items.titleZh: 报道称，任天堂ROM芯片供应商旺宏退出，转而专注AI数据中心芯片
items.descriptionZh:
据报道，任天堂Switch和Switch 2游戏卡带的关键ROM芯片供应商之一旺宏电子（Macronix）正在逐步退出ROM业务，将制造重心转向NOR和NAND闪存，以供应快速扩张的AI数据中心。这一变化并非芯片技术本身的突破，而是存储产业产能重新配置的结果：AI数据中心对内存和存储的需求正在吞噬全球供应，使传统游戏卡带所需的ROM芯片在商业上变得不再优先。若消息属实，任天堂可能面临卡带成本上升、增加Game-Key卡（仅含下载密钥而非完整游戏）或进一步倾向数字销售的壓力，物理游戏的前景也因此再添不确定性。

从背景看，旺宏是任天堂Switch 1和Switch 2游戏存储卡中ROM芯片的主要制造商之一。MST Financial分析师David Gibson在社交平台X上指出，旺宏正在淘汰该业务，不会推出新的ROM产品，今年第三季度将是其最后一次单独报告ROM销售。数据显示，旺宏ROM销售占比已从去年的26%降至今年第三季度的5%。同时，该公司新台币378亿元资本支出全部投向NOR和NAND闪存，没有留给ROM；《台北时报》也印证了这一方向，称旺宏正逐步退出ROM生产。其资本支出分两阶段：先以新台币220亿元扩大制造产能，再追加新台币158亿元用于eMMC所需的NAND闪存和3D NAND。换言之，旺宏把有限产能从低增长、低利润的游戏卡带ROM转向AI数据中心所需的高价值存储产品。

这一供应链调整的影响需要从任天堂的卡带供应结构理解。任天堂并不直接向旺宏采购ROM芯片，而是由无晶圆厂芯片设计公司MegaChips根据任天堂需求设计ROM芯片，再外包给旺宏制造。MegaChips 2022年公司报告显示，任天堂占其销售额的87.8%，旺宏占其外包制造采购的67.8%；报告甚至警告，如果旺宏无法制造ROM芯片，“MegaChips的经营业绩可能受到影响”。当时这一风险尚未显现，如今却变得非常现实，而外界尚不清楚MegaChips有何应急预案。不过，旺宏与MegaChips很可能已就退出计划进行沟通，并给后者留出寻找替代制造商的时间。Gibson认为，由于旺宏并非任天堂唯一的游戏存储卡制造商，ROHM Semiconductor和LAPIS Semiconductor仍在向任天堂供应ROM芯片，物理卡带“可能还会持续一段时间”；但在边际上，数字销售会通过更多Game-Key卡和纯数字销售继续增长，任天堂的数字利润率也有望缓慢上升，具体数字会因重大实体游戏发售而按季度波动。

从性能和产业对比看，ROM芯片本身通常用于固化游戏数据，成本敏感、容量和读写需求相对固定；NOR和NAND闪存则面向代码存储、嵌入式存储和大容量数据存储，尤其3D NAND和用于eMMC的NAND在数据中心、移动设备和嵌入式市场具有更高附加值和更大需求。旺宏将新台币378亿元资本支出全部转向NOR/NAND，意味着其ROM业务已不再是战略重点；ROM销售占比从26%降至5%也说明该业务规模正在快速萎缩。对任天堂而言，少一个关键供应商可能推高物理游戏价格，或迫使公司生产更多Game-Key卡、扩大数字发行。对MegaChips而言，风险更为集中：任天堂贡献其近九成销售额，而旺宏又承担其近七成外包制造采购，一旦替代代工安排不能及时落地，其经营将受到明显冲击。总体来看，这一事件是全球存储产能向AI数据中心倾斜的缩影，短期内物理游戏不会立即消失，但实体卡带的成本、供应稳定性和数字化的相对吸引力都将发生变化。

items.content: Data center developers are poised to face a more restrictive building environment after voters across the country voted in candidates who favor moratoriums and ballot measures that put more obstacles on their expansion, delivering a stinging blow to a central pillar of the AI industry.Of voters polled by NBC News on Election Day, 76 percent said they opposed data centers in their communities. Dozens of local communities voted directly to restrict development through ballot measures. And upset winners like Texas Democratic Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa and Michigan’s Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed support moratoriums on development.It’s hard to draw a direct line from data center backlash to the election of any of these candidates, and there were still some races where candidates who favored more limited restrictions on data centers prevailed. Republican Rep. Byron Donalds, who previously lauded development in Florida, was elected as governor, and Iowa’s Democratic Governor-elect Rob Sand opposed a moratorium that his challenger favored. But even these candidates were forced to engage on data center issues during their campaigns, and will be likely to face continued pressure to put at least some guardrails in place.Ballot measuresVoters were faced with questions about data centers directly in 45 local ballot measures nationwide. As of Wednesday morning, according to a site compiled by Redbud Consulting, the results of 33 of those will restrict data center development. The Town of Wells, Maine, favored a 180-day moratorium on large data centers, backdated to mid-June 2026. Several cities in Ohio voted to ban data centers over 25MW. The City of El Dorado, Kansas, voted to ban data centers with peak electrical load over 10MW for 10 years.Dozens of local communities voted directly to restrict developmentTexasDemocratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa will take over the governor’s seat from Republican incumbent Greg Abbott, marking a major Democratic flip in a state with the second-highest number of planned data centers. Hinojosa supports a statewide moratorium on data center development, while Abbott took a more measured approach. He announced a new audit this summer on data centers that could slow new developments from connecting to the state energy grid, but has previously praised data center expansion in the state.In another major upset, Democratic State Rep. James Talarico flipped Texas blue in a landmark Senate victory against Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton. Both Talarico and Paxton wanted to remove some tax exemptions for data centers, and to make them responsible for their own energy infrastructure-related costs. But Talarico also put an emphasis on the facilities’ environmental impact and ensuring they shared their profits with the public, while Paxton’s message focused on keeping Chinese tech out of data centers.FloridaRepublican congressman Byron Donalds won the governor’s seat over Democratic former congressman David Jolly. Donalds opposed an outright ban of data centers, while Jolly said he’d bar hyperscalers for a year beginning on day one in office. In Congress, Donalds introduced the Protecting Ratepayers Act, which would make developers pay for their own energy and water needs. Donalds’ win was still closer than expected in a state that’s been a Republican stronghold in the Trump era. As of Wednesday morning, NBC News reported that Donalds had exactly 50 percent of the vote, with 99 percent of expected votes already counted, while Jolly had 48.7 percent, and the rest went to an Independent candidate.PennsylvaniaDemocratic incumbent Governor Josh Shapiro held onto his seat against Republican challenger and state Treasurer Stacy Garrity. Both Shapiro and Garrity toughened their stances against data centers as the race went on, despite previously touting their potential benefits to the state. Shapiro signed an executive order that barred nondisclosure agreements for data center developments and took proposals for AI data centers off the fast track. Garrity has said she supports a development pause of up to three years.OhioDemocrat Sherrod Brown won back his former Senate seat from Republican incumbent Jon Husted, whom Brown had labeled “the face of data centers.” The National Republican Senatorial Committee warned this summer in a leaked memo that if data centers were blamed for Husted’s potential loss, it would make them seem poisonous to future candidates. Husted earlier helped install data center tax breaks as lieutenant governor, though he more recently introduced the Ratepayer Protection Act in Congress to force large data centers to cover their infrastructure upgrade and energy costs. Brown hammered Husted on the issue throughout the campaign, and while he hasn’t gone as far as to call for a moratorium, he’s said that developers shouldn’t get tax breaks or get a go-ahead without local input.Republicans warned that if data centers were blamed for Husted’s potential loss, it would make them seem poisonous to future candidatesMichiganDemocrat and former public health official Abdul El-Sayed won the Senate race over Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers. El-Sayed was one of the earliest politicians to stake his position on data centers, and has called for a pause on new developments “until we can do it safely and with federal protections.” Rogers called for a one-year state moratorium this summer, but not a federal ban.As of Wednesday morning, NBC News had not yet called a House race between Democratic organizer William Lawrence and Republican incumbent Tom Barrett, but Lawrence held a lead with 92 percent of the vote in. Similar to El-Sayed, Lawrence stated his position on data centers early on, calling for a one-year federal moratorium on new developments during his primary campaign. Barrett introduced legislation this summer to bar nondisclosure agreements for data center developments and give locals more control.MaineDemocrat and former Maine State Senator Troy Jackson ousted Republican Sen. Susan Collins from her Senate seat. The state legislature passed what would have been the country’s first moratorium on data centers, had the governor not vetoed it. But polls show that opposition to data centers among Maine residents remained strong. Jackson supported a state moratorium on data centers, while Collins opposed such a measure but called for more local control and protection for energy ratepayers.WisconsinDemocratic Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley won the governor’s race over Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany. Neither Crowley nor Tiffany favored a moratorium on data centers, and have distanced themselves from previous support. Crowley won his primary over progressive primary opponent Francesca Hong, who supported a moratorium. Both Crowley and Tiffany said they wanted to end state tax subsidies for data centers though they’ve accused one another of flip-flopping their stances.NevadaDemocratic Attorney General Aaron Ford successfully flipped the governor’s seat from incumbent Republican Joe Lombardo, whom he’d branded “data center Joe.” Lombardo has previously made supportive comments about data centers, but more recently introduced an executive order making tax incentives contingent on data centers covering power costs and meeting certain environmental standards. Ford previously championed a 2015 data center tax-break bill, but said today’s data centers are different from those years ago, and now supports a pause on all tax breaks for new data centers.GeorgiaDemocrat and former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms won the Georgia governor’s seat over Republican healthcare executive Rick Jackson. Bottoms favored a moratorium on data centers to review environmental and cost effects, while Jackson preferred to leave decisions up to locals.ArizonaDemocratic Gov. Katie Hobbs fought off a challenge from Republican Rep. Andy Biggs. Both opposed a moratorium on data centers in favor of power and water use standards.Democratic Attorney General Kris Mayes held onto her seat over a challenge from Republican state legislator Warren Petersen. Mayes took a more hardline view than her Democratic peer, Hobbs, by endorsing a state moratorium on data center development. Petersen opposed a moratorium, and said data centers are necessary for technology residents use every day.IowaDemocratic state auditor Rob Sand won the governor’s seat over Republican businessman Zach Lahn. Sand did not support a data center moratorium, which Lahn did. But both agreed on ending tax breaks for the developments.South CarolinaDemocratic pediatrician Annie Andrews flipped South Carolina’s Senate seat blue in a race against Republican incumbent Darline Graham, who had taken over the seat after her brother Lindsey Graham died. Andrews supported a two-year data center moratorium, while Graham opposed a pause and got significant support from a super PAC allied with the data center industry.

items.titleZh: 数据中心在中期选举中失利
items.descriptionZh:
美国本轮选举结果显示，数据中心开发商将面对更严格的建设环境：多地选民选出支持暂停令和公投限制的候选人，并通过地方公投直接收紧数据中心扩张。这被视为对AI产业核心基础设施支柱的一次重挫。NBC News选举日民调显示，76%的受访者反对在所在社区建设数据中心；数十个地方社区通过 ballot measures 直接限制开发。尽管很难把数据中心反弹直接等同于某些候选人的胜选原因，而且仍有部分对数据中心限制较温和的候选人获胜，但即便是这些候选人也被迫在竞选中回应数据中心议题，未来仍将面临设置监管护栏的压力。

从技术背景看，AI数据中心是承载大规模GPU/加速卡集群、高速网络和存储的算力基础设施，功率密度远高于传统机房，需要大规模电力接入、冷却和水资源。新闻中的25MW、10MW等门槛指峰值电力负荷，大致对应大型和中型数据中心规模。政策工具包括暂停新开发、公投禁令、峰值负荷上限、取消税收优惠、要求开发商承担电网和水源升级成本、禁止保密协议、将AI数据中心移出快速审批通道、制定“费率保护”立法，以及把税收激励与电力成本、环境和水资源标准挂钩。这些措施并不直接改变AI芯片技术，但会通过选址、并网、融资和建设周期约束AI算力的落地速度。

地方公投方面，全国共有45项直接涉及数据中心的公投；截至周三上午，据Redbud Consulting汇编，其中33项结果将限制数据中心开发，约占七成。缅因州Wells镇支持对大型数据中心实施180天暂停令，并回溯至2026年6月中旬；俄亥俄州多个城市投票禁止超过25MW的数据中心；堪萨斯州El Dorado市投票禁止峰值电力负荷超过10MW的数据中心，期限10年。

各州选情呈现广泛收紧态势。得克萨斯州民主党人Gina Hinojosa赢得州长席位，接替共和党现任州长Greg Abbott。得州计划数据中心数量位居全美第二；Hinojosa支持全州暂停数据中心开发，Abbott则采取较温和路线，今夏宣布对新数据中心进行审计，可能放缓其接入州电网，但此前曾赞扬数据中心扩张。另一场重大翻盘中，民主党州众议员James Talarico击败州总检察长Ken Paxton赢得参议院席位。两人都希望取消部分数据中心税收豁免，并让数据中心承担自身能源基础设施相关成本；Talarico更强调环境影响和与公众分享利润，Paxton则聚焦阻止中国技术进入数据中心。

佛罗里达州共和党众议员Byron Donalds击败民主党前众议员David Jolly赢得州长席位。Donalds反对全面禁止数据中心，Jolly则称上任第一天起将禁止超大规模云服务商一年。Donalds在国会提出《保护费率纳税人法案》，要求开发商自行承担能源和水需求。尽管佛州在特朗普时代是共和党票仓，Donalds胜幅仍小于预期：截至周三上午，NBC News称在99%预期选票已统计情况下，Donalds恰为50%，Jolly为48.7%，其余流向独立候选人。

宾夕法尼亚州民主党现任州长Josh Shapiro击败共和党州财政部长Stacy Garrity。两人在选战中均强化了对数据中心的强硬立场，尽管此前曾宣传其潜在收益。Shapiro签署行政令，禁止数据中心开发保密协议，并将AI数据中心提案移出快速审批通道；Garrity表示支持最长三年的开发暂停。俄亥俄州民主党人Sherrod Brown从共和党现任参议员Jon Husted手中夺回参议院席位，Brown曾称Husted是“数据中心的面孔”。全国共和党参议院委员会今夏一份泄露备忘录警告，若数据中心被归咎于Husted潜在败选，将使该议题对未来候选人“有毒”。Husted任副州长时曾帮助设立数据中心税收优惠，但近期在国会提出《费率纳税人保护法案》，迫使大型数据中心承担基础设施升级和能源成本。Brown在竞选中持续攻击该议题，虽未呼吁暂停令，但表示开发商不应获得税收优惠，也不应在没有地方意见的情况下获批。

密歇根州民主党人、前公共卫生官员Abdul El-Sayed击败共和党前众议员Mike Rogers赢得参议院席位。El-Sayed是最早明确数据中心立场的政客之一，呼吁暂停新开发，“直到我们能安全推进并获得联邦保护”。Rogers今夏呼吁州级暂停一年，但不支持联邦禁令。截至周三上午，NBC News尚未宣布民主党组织者William Lawrence与共和党现任众议员Tom Barrett之间的众议院选情，但Lawrence在92%选票统计下领先。与El-Sayed类似，Lawrence初选期间即呼吁联邦暂停新数据中心一年；Barrett今夏提出立法，禁止数据中心开发保密协议并赋予地方更多控制权。

缅因州民主党人、前州参议员Troy Jackson击败共和党参议员Susan Collins赢得参议院席位。该州立法机构曾通过全国首个数据中心暂停令，但被州长否决；民调显示缅因居民对数据中心的反对仍强。Jackson支持州级暂停令，Collins反对暂停但呼吁更多地方控制和对能源费率纳税人的保护。威斯康星州民主党人、密尔沃基县行政长官David Crowley击败共和党众议员Tom Tiffany赢得州长席位。两人都不支持暂停令，并与此前支持立场保持距离；Crowley初选击败支持暂停令的进步派对手Francesca Hong。两人均表示希望终止州级数据中心税收补贴，但互相指责立场反复。内华达州民主党总检察长Aaron Ford击败共和党现任州长Joe Lombardo，Ford曾称后者为“数据中心Joe”。Lombardo此前对数据中心发表支持言论，但近期签署行政令，使税收激励取决于数据中心承担电力成本并满足环境标准。Ford曾推动2015年数据中心税收优惠法案，但称今天的数据中心与当年不同，现在支持暂停对所有新数据中心的税收优惠。

佐治亚州民主党人、前亚特兰大市长Keisha Lance Bottoms击败共和党医疗高管Rick Jackson赢得州长席位。Bottoms支持暂停数据中心以审查环境和成本影响，Jackson倾向于由地方决定。亚利桑那州民主党州长Katie Hobbs击退共和党众议员Andy Biggs挑战；两人都反对暂停令，支持电力和用水标准。民主党总检察长Kris Mayes击败共和党州议员Warren Petersen保住席位；Mayes比Hobbs更强硬，支持州级暂停数据中心开发，Petersen反对暂停并称数据中心是居民日常技术所必需。艾奥瓦州民主党州审计长Rob Sand击败共和党商人Zach Lahn赢得州长席位。Sand不支持数据中心暂停令，Lahn支持；两人都同意终止税收优惠。南卡罗来纳州民主党儿科医生Annie Andrews击败共和党现任参议员Darline Graham翻蓝参议院席位；Andrews支持两年数据中心暂停令，Graham反对暂停，并获得与数据中心行业结盟的超级政治行动委员会大力支持。

总体看，数据中心议题已从地方规划问题上升为选举议题，政策呈现碎片化收紧：暂停令、峰值负荷限制、取消税收优惠、强制承担电网成本、禁止保密协议和加强地方控制成为主要工具。对AI产业而言，超大规模训练集群、云推理和企业AI部署都依赖可落地的高功率数据中心；限制将推高选址、并网和融资的不确定性，延长建设周期，并可能促使开发商转向政策友好地区，采用自备电源、长期购电协议、储能、液冷和更高能效方案，同时通过社区利益分享和公开承诺缓和反对。短期内，AI算力扩张成本和节奏将受基础设施约束；长期则可能形成更分散、更本地化的数据中心政策格局，AI芯片和服务器需求仍将增长，但其部署速度更取决于电力、土地和社区许可能否同步落地。

items.title: Micron details ambitious DRAM and NAND roadmap — 3D NAND, High-NA EUV, new materials, and custom silicon makes a comeback
items.description: As DRAM and 3D NAND are about to adopt all-new technologies, custom types of memory are about to become mainstream as AI developers face limitations with current solutions.
items.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Last month, Micron disclosed its DRAM and NAND memory roadmaps for the next several years, revealing plans to use wafer bonding, new materials that enable making NAND cells smaller, High-NA EUV lithography, and detailing its moves toward 3D DRAM. Perhaps the most revealing part of Micron's story is that the company plans to expand its portfolio of custom DRAM and NAND products as AI developers increasingly require memory and storage solutions optimized for their unique processor architectures and specific workloads. (Image credit: Micron)" DRAM is nearing atomic limits at this point: although we have confidence in several more planar nodes, we are very focused on making sure that we introduce 3D DRAM at the optimal time from a cost and performance point of view," said Scott DeBoer, president and chief technology and products officer at Micron, at the company's event earlier this month. "[With 3D NAND, we are] really focused on new materials densifying the cell architecture, and continuing to focus on that XYZ scaling going forward."DRAM: 4F2 cells axed, High-NA EUV lithography, new materials, and 3D DRAM enable future scalingIn a surprising move, Micron decided to abandon plans to produce DRAM with 4F2 memory cells, unlike its rivals at CXMT, Samsung, and SK hynix, citing the lack of a viable scaling path beyond where Micron is today. Instead, Micron's roadmap for the coming years includes wafer bonding, High-NA EUV lithography, new materials, and eventually 3D DRAM. The company plans to begin mass production of its next-generation 1δ memory in the second half of 2027, while subsequent 1ε, ζÅ, and ηÅ technologies are at various stages of development. In parallel, Micron is developing two generations of 3D DRAM that could eventually succeed conventional planar memory.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Micron)Micron's current 1γ (1-gamma) DRAM process technology, which is in high-volume manufacturing (HVM), is the company's first DRAM node to use EUV lithography. Previously, Micron had used multipatterning with DUV lithography and remained competitive with Samsung and SK hynix, which relied on EUV for critical layers.Micron's next-generation 1δ (1-delta) fabrication process is currently in the yield ramp stage and is scheduled to enter mass production in the second half of 2027. The company expects the technology to increase bit density by mid-20% compared to 1γ, while advanced high-k metal gate (HKMG) CMOS, new materials, angstrom-level process control, and equipment intelligence should improve performance, power efficiency, and ultimately yields as well as costs. You may like Micron plans to use wafer bonding and High-NA EUV for next-gen DRAM Micron's next-generation 3D NAND to double bit density with over 400 layers, offering extreme performance Hot Chips 2026: d-Matrix stacks AI accelerator directly on custom DRAM for 100 TB/s per card (Image credit: Micron)Micron plans to manufacture 1δ DRAM in the U.S. and use the technology for next-generation DDR, LPDDR, graphics memory, HBM5, vertical HBM (vHBM), and vertical Edge Inference Memory (vEIM) products. Meanwhile, to make HBM5, vHBM5, and vEIM products, the node will also support additional features like through-silicon vias (TSVs) and other elements to improve thermal performance.The subsequent 1ε (1-epsilon) process will rely on wafer bonding, which will enable Micron to produce different structures on separate wafers and then bond them together. This approach could increase flexibility in memory design and manufacturing, but Micron has yet to disclose its plans to implement wafer bonding, which structures it will bond, or what improvements in density, performance, and power consumption the technology will provide. The process is currently under development, and there is no announced production schedule.Micron's ζÅ (zeta-angstrom) production node is currently in early development and will introduce High-NA EUV lithography to memory manufacturing, which will enable further reductions in critical dimensions. The company has not disclosed how many layers will require High-NA lithography, the expected density improvements, or when the technology will enter mass production. However, it is obvious that the node will not be here until at least 2030, years after Samsung and SK hynix adopt High-NA EUV at their DRAM fabs (planned for 2028).The ηÅ (eta-angstrom) process represents the most distant generation on Micron’s disclosed planar DRAM roadmap and is currently in the pathfinding stage. After Micron inserts High-NA EUV lithography into its DRAM production flow, the company intends to bet on other methods of scaling. Although Micron mentions new materials, it hasn't identified them or explained how they will affect device structures. These could include new photoresists, deposition precursors, dielectric materials, or conductive materials that would enable the company to manufacture smaller transistors and capacitors, and ultimately increase DRAM cell density.In any case, Micron's roadmap is focused on continuing development of DRAM based on 6F² cells, which differs from the plans of CXMT, Samsung, and SK hynix. What to read next Micron pulls the plug on future 4F² DRAM after two decades of research in dramatic shift Samsung reveals a three-phase HBM roadmap that puts logic and compute inside memory — zHBM ultimately stacks DRAM directly on top of the processor Hot Chips 2026: Micron warns HBM wafer penalty is widening with every generation 3D1 and 3D2: Transition to 3D DRAM is loomingIn parallel with conventional DRAM development, Micron is working on two generations of 3D DRAM, currently called 3D1 and 3D2. Unlike planar DRAM, which primarily relies on smaller memory cells to increase bit density, 3D DRAM would use the vertical dimension to accommodate more memory cells within a given area. Micron intends to introduce the technology when it becomes competitive with conventional DRAM in terms of manufacturing costs and performance. The company has not disclosed architectures, layer counts, or density targets.In fact, while Micron has outlined its future memory architectures through 2030, its DRAM manufacturing roadmap provides a firm production window only for the 1δ process, which is scheduled to enter high-volume manufacturing in the second half of 2027. The company has not disclosed production dates for subsequent planar DRAM nodes or either generation of 3D DRAM.Custom HBM and vertical memory architecturesIn addition to conventional DRAM, Micron plans to use its future manufacturing technologies for HBM4E, HBM5, HBM5E, and new vertically integrated memory architectures. Starting with HBM4E, the company will offer both standard and custom HBM products, which will be followed by custom HBM5E, vHBM, and vEIM (vertical Edge Inference Memory). All of these will mark the re-emergence of custom memory in mass-produced products. (Image credit: Micron)Custom HBM4E (cHBM4E) will enable Micron's customers to shrink memory I/O width and/or integrate additional logic into the memory's base die to free up valuable die space for compute and optimize performance and power consumption for specific AI accelerators. According to Scott DeBoer, Micron’s president and chief technology and products officer, some of these functions would otherwise reside in the ASIC itself, so moving them closer to memory should improve overall system efficiency."When we co-design a base die, and the certain logic elements that are desired to be put in that base die are generally an offload from GPU circuitry anyway onto the base die to put it closer to the memory," said DeBoer. "Moving what makes more sense onto the base die will still be a reality in [the] vertical HBM timeframe as well."To support these capabilities, Micron intends to use advanced foundry process technologies for the base dies of both standard and custom HBM products, although it has not disclosed specific nodes. For custom designs, the company will select the most cost-effective process that meets customer requirements. For example, Micron expects HBM4E to require more advanced CMOS technologies to meet its performance and power targets. (Image credit: Micron)Further down the road, Micron intends to introduce vertical HBM (vHBM), which will stack memory directly on top of ASICs and CPUs rather than next to them on an interposer. This architecture promises substantially higher bandwidth, thanks to dense vertical connections (as well as significantly lower latencies) thanks to adjacent placement, but it is also set to create considerable challenges related to power delivery and heat dissipation. To address them, Micron plans to use hybrid bonding for advanced interconnects, integrated heat spreaders, and thermally aware designs. Interestingly, the company expects conventional HBM and vHBM to coexist in some designs, where vHBM provides maximum bandwidth, while traditional HBM serves capacity requirements.Another technology under development is vertical Edge Inference Memory (vEIM), which shares many of its packaging and integration technologies with HBM, but targets applications that require power efficiency more than maximum bandwidth. Micron's 1st Generation vEIM aims to deliver formidable HBM4-like 2 TB/s of bandwidth while consuming less than 1 picojoule per bit of data transfer energy.Both architectures will require close cooperation with customers to optimize memory, logic, packaging, and thermal characteristics for particular applications, so Micron will need to work with its clients to make vHBM and vEIM successful. Interestingly, Micron's customer-specific development efforts extend beyond HBM and EIM. (Image credit: Micron)For example, the company is collaborating with Meta to optimize LPDDR6 for data center applications, which primarily include reliability, serviceability, and availability. Micron expects LPDDR6 to reduce power consumption by approximately 35% compared to LPDDR5, which will be very important for dense memory deployments. The company also intends to develop DDR6 — which targets 2X DDR5 bandwidth — in cooperation with major customers to better understand and ultimately meet their needs.Speaking of customer cooperation, DeBoer stresses that Micron now collaborates with customers from the earliest stages of product definition through joint design, development, validation, and volume production. According to the executive, this approach differs substantially from how the company worked with customers previously."Across our AI co-invention opportunities we are co-imagining, co-designing, co-developing, co-validating, and then delivering at scale," DeBoer said. "This opportunity is truly unique. It is very different than the way we interacted with customers even three or four years ago."Advanced CMOS: More than 10X performance improvementIn addition to shrinking DRAM cells and developing vertical memory architectures, Micron is developing advanced CMOS technologies for peripheral circuitry. The company's roadmap includes several generations of DRAM CMOS logic with high-k metal gate transistors, followed by 1st and 2nd Generation 3D CMOS technologies.Micron expects these advances to increase its CMOS logic performance by more than 10X between 2020 and 2030, which should help the company address the growing bandwidth and power requirements of AI-oriented memory products.3D NAND: From next-gen 400L 3D NAND to AI-oriented NANDAlthough Micron's event was mostly dedicated to the future of DRAM, the company also shared some details about its upcoming NAND innovations, which include 11th Generation 3D NAND with 400 layers, post-G11 3D NAND, and AI-oriented NAND memory that either offers high bandwidth or high IOPS.Micron's next-generation G11 (N170) 3D NAND technology represents a substantial departure from its current G9 (N160) process. The company plans to increase the number of active memory layers from 276 to more than 400, introduce wafer-on-wafer bonding, and implement an industry-leading memory cell pitch.These improvements are expected to double the bit density of G11 3D NAND compared with G9 3D NAND, presumably from 21 Gb/mm2 to 42 Gb/mm2 in the case of 3D TLC devices, which should substantially reduce manufacturing costs per bit once the technology reaches mature yields. (Image credit: Micron)In addition to increased storage density, G11 also targets a 50% increase in I/O speed compared with G9, which implies a potential transfer rate of approximately 5,400 MT/s. Furthermore, Micron expects to reduce data transfer energy consumption by more than 25% per bit, an important improvement for high-capacity SSDs and AI storage systems that tend to move huge amounts of data.One of the most important changes with G11 is the adoption of wafer-on-wafer bonding, which lets Micron manufacture memory arrays and the periphery and I/O circuits on another wafer, then bond them together. Chinese manufacturer YMTC has used this method to maximize storage capacity and performance, so it is not surprising that Micron and other memory manufacturers are adopting the technique as well.Micron expects to start mass production of G11 3D NAND in the second half of 2027.Improving 3D NAND past G11: New materials and further XYZ scalingMicron intends to continue improving 3D NAND beyond 11th Generation through a combination of new materials, denser memory cell architectures, and more energy-efficient devices and data paths. Specifically, Micron is investigating high-mobility materials that could improve the electrical characteristics of future memory devices, as well as ultra-dense cell architectures intended to increase storage density beyond what an increase in active layers provides.Meanwhile, more energy-efficient circuitry and data paths should help offset the growing power consumption associated with higher NAND capacities and faster interfaces. (Image credit: Micron)"Beyond G11, we have a strong roadmap, not going to go into great detail on it today, but really focused on new materials densifying the cell architecture, and continuing to focus on that XYZ scaling going forward," said DeBoer. "[…] The current industry direction and Micron’s direction is scaling both by adding layers [and] also by shrinking the cell dimensions."The company has not identified the materials it intends to introduce or explained how they will affect memory cell structures. Nor has it provided quantitative density, performance, or power targets for NAND generations beyond G11.AI-oriented NAND: Higher IOPS and bandwidthAlthough Micron is not ready to share details about its G12 or G13 3D NAND generations, the company disclosed that it is developing two specialized NAND architectures for AI applications.The first — High-IOPS AI NAND — architecture focuses on maximum random I/O performance and uses SLC-based designs with small blocks to accelerate workloads such as vector searches, graph analytics, and AI context management. Micron envisions products capable of delivering approximately 25 million to 100 million IOPS, depending on their configuration, and expects to bring products based on this approach to market over the next couple of years. (Image credit: Micron)The second — High-Bandwidth AI NAND — architecture prioritizes bandwidth over random I/O performance. Micron is investigating vertically stacked NAND devices connected through TSVs and equipped with a logic base die that resides close to AI accelerators, so from many points of view this concept resembles SanDisk's HBF. However, Micron does not believe that simply placing NAND stacks alongside AI accelerators on an interposer offers sufficient advantages. Instead, the company is exploring alternative integration approaches that bring NAND closer to compute resources, but don't necessarily consume valuable shoreline (the perimeter, or edge) of AI accelerators."[The High-Bandwidth AI NAND is] more costly and has to be implemented in partnership with customers in a way to ensure that they are meeting the mark and the cost point to drive the value proposition," DeBoer said. "We are enabling TSV-stacked NAND with a logic base die to bring memory closer to accelerators. We do not think placing it along the shoreline of the GPU has merit. Instead, we want to position it closer to the compute itself to take advantage of this high-performance NAND." (Image credit: Micron)These specialized AI-focused NAND architectures will complement Micron's conventional SSD roadmap, which includes plans for drives with capacities of up to 512 TB in the foreseeable future.

items.titleZh: 美光详述雄心勃勃的DRAM与NAND路线图——3D NAND、高数值孔径EUV、新材料，以及定制芯片卷土重来
items.descriptionZh:
美光在近期技术路线图活动上公布了未来数年的DRAM与NAND存储路线图，核心方向包括晶圆键合、使NAND单元进一步缩小的新材料、High-NA EUV光刻，以及向3D DRAM过渡。最引人注目的是，美光计划扩大定制DRAM和NAND产品组合，因为AI开发者越来越需要针对其独特处理器架构和特定工作负载优化的内存与存储方案。

在DRAM方面，美光总裁兼首席技术与产品官Scott DeBoer表示，DRAM已接近原子极限，公司虽对后续若干平面节点仍有信心，但更关注在成本与性能最合适的时机推出3D DRAM。美光出人意料地放弃了4F² DRAM单元方案，理由是该方案缺乏可行的进一步缩放路径；这与长鑫存储、三星和SK海力士继续推进4F²的路线不同。美光将继续基于6F²单元发展DRAM。其当前1γ（1-gamma）节点已进入高量产，是美光首个使用EUV光刻的DRAM节点；此前美光依靠DUV多重曝光仍与三星、SK海力士保持竞争。下一代1δ（1-delta）处于良率爬坡阶段，计划2027年下半年量产，比特密度预计较1γ提升约20%多，并通过先进高k金属栅HKMG CMOS、新材料、埃级工艺控制和设备智能改善性能、能效、良率与成本。美光计划在美国制造1δ，并将其用于下一代DDR、LPDDR、图形内存、HBM5、垂直HBM（vHBM）和垂直边缘推理内存（vEIM）等产品；为制造HBM5、vHBM和vEIM，该节点还将支持TSV等改善散热的功能。

后续1ε（1-epsilon）工艺将采用晶圆键合，可在不同晶圆上制造不同结构再键合，从而增加内存设计与制造灵活性，但美光尚未披露键合结构、密度/性能/功耗改进及生产计划。ζÅ（zeta-angstrom）节点处于早期开发阶段，将把High-NA EUV引入内存制造以进一步缩小关键尺寸，但未披露层数、密度提升和量产时间；外界预计至少到2030年，晚于三星和SK海力士计划2028年采用High-NA EUV。ηÅ（eta-angstrom）是美光披露的平面DRAM路线图中最远的一代，处于路径探索阶段，计划在引入High-NA EUV后依靠其他缩放方法，新材料可能包括新光刻胶、沉积前驱体、介电材料或导电材料，以制造更小晶体管和电容、提高DRAM单元密度。与此同时，美光还在开发3D1和3D2两代3D DRAM，利用垂直维度在给定面积内容纳更多存储单元，并计划在制造成本和性能可与传统DRAM竞争时推出；但未披露架构、层数和密度目标。整体看，美光DRAM路线图中只有1δ有明确量产窗口，后续平面节点和3D DRAM均无明确日期。

在定制HBM和垂直存储架构方面，美光计划将未来制造技术用于HBM4E、HBM5、HBM5E及新型垂直集成存储架构。从HBM4E开始，美光将同时提供标准和定制HBM产品，后续还有定制HBM5E、vHBM和vEIM，这标志着定制内存在大规模量产产品中的回归。定制HBM4E可让客户缩小内存I/O宽度和/或在内存基础die中集成额外逻辑，为计算芯片释放宝贵die面积，并针对特定AI加速器优化性能与功耗。DeBoer称，这些逻辑原本多位于ASIC中，将其移到更靠近内存的基础die上有助提升系统效率；在垂直HBM时代，把更适合的逻辑移到基础die上仍会实现。美光将为标准和定制HBM的基础die采用先进代工工艺，但未披露具体节点；定制设计将选择满足客户需求且成本效益最高的工艺。HBM4E预计需要更先进CMOS以满足性能和功耗目标。更远期，美光将推出vHBM，把内存直接堆叠在ASIC和CPU之上，而非放在中介层旁边。该架构通过密集垂直连接有望显著提高带宽并降低延迟，但供电和散热挑战很大；美光计划采用混合键合、集成热扩散器和热感知设计应对，并预计传统HBM与vHBM会在部分设计中共存，vHBM提供最大带宽，传统HBM满足容量需求。另一项vEIM共享HBM的许多封装与集成技术，但更强调能效而非最大带宽，第一代目标提供类似HBM4的2 TB/s带宽，同时每比特数据传输能耗低于1皮焦。

美光还在与Meta合作优化面向数据中心应用的LPDDR6，重点包括可靠性、可服务性和可用性；预计LPDDR6较LPDDR5降低约35%功耗，这对密集内存部署很重要。美光还计划与主要客户合作开发DDR6，目标是达到DDR5的两倍带宽。DeBoer强调，美光现在从产品定义最早阶段就与客户合作，贯穿联合设计、开发、验证和量产，这种“共同想象、共同设计、共同开发、共同验证并规模化交付”的方式与三四年前明显不同。在先进CMOS方面，美光路线图包括多代采用HKMG晶体管的DRAM CMOS逻辑，随后是第一代和第二代3D CMOS，预计2020年至2030年间CMOS逻辑性能提升10倍以上，以应对AI导向内存产品不断增长的带宽和功耗需求。

NAND方面，美光下一代G11（N170）3D NAND较当前G9（N160）有重大变化：活动存储层从276层增至400层以上，引入晶圆对晶圆键合，并采用业界领先的存储单元间距。美光预计G11比特密度较G9翻倍，3D TLC器件可能从21 Gb/mm²提升至42 Gb/mm²，从而在成熟良率下显著降低每比特制造成本；同时I/O速度目标较G9提升50%，潜在传输速率约5,400 MT/s，每比特数据传输能耗降低25%以上，这对高容量SSD和AI存储系统很重要。G11采用晶圆对晶圆键合，可在另一晶圆上制造存储阵列以及外围和I/O电路再键合；长江存储曾用类似方法最大化容量和性能。美光计划2027年下半年量产G11。G11之后，美光将通过新材料、更致密存储单元架构、更节能器件和数据路径继续改进3D NAND，正在研究可改善未来器件电特性的高迁移率材料，以及超越增加有源层数量的超致密单元架构，并继续推进XYZ缩放；但未披露具体材料、量化密度/性能/功耗目标。

针对AI应用，美光还在开发两种专用NAND架构。第一种High-IOPS AI NAND侧重最大随机I/O性能，采用基于SLC的小块设计，加速向量搜索、图分析和AI上下文管理等负载，预计可提供约2500万至1亿IOPS，未来几年推向市场。第二种High-Bandwidth AI NAND优先带宽，研究通过TSV连接的垂直堆叠NAND并配备靠近AI加速器的逻辑基础die，概念上类似SanDisk的HBF；但美光认为简单把NAND堆栈放在中介层上、沿AI加速器 shoreline 布置优势不足，正探索让NAND更靠近计算资源又不占用加速器宝贵边缘的集成方式。该方案成本更高，需与客户合作确保达到价值和成本点。这些AI专用NAND将与美光传统SSD路线图互补，后者计划在可预见未来推出容量最高512 TB的SSD。

总体来看，美光路线图反映出存储产业正从单纯缩小单元转向材料、键合、3D堆叠、High-NA EUV和定制化架构并重。对AI系统而言，定制HBM、vHBM、vEIM、高IOPS/高带宽NAND以及数据中心LPDDR6等产品，将分别面向训练/推理加速器的高带宽低延迟、边缘推理的高能效、AI存储的高吞吐与高随机访问等场景，推动内存与计算更紧密协同设计。

items.title: AI data centers comprehensively defeated at US midterm elections — 45 measures put on the ballot as Americans overwhelmingly vote against developments
items.description: Several counties put data center issues on the ballot during the midterm elections, with most Americans voting against data center development in their county.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 12 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Several counties in the U.S. have put data center concerns on the midterm ballot, and early results show that Americans are overwhelmingly voting against them. According to Data Centers on the Ballot, 33 measures restricting data center development have already won, with six more questions leading. Only one measure in Harwood, North Dakota, which adds an extra review process for industrial projects, including data centers, has failed, while a further five have no posted results. This is a major setback for the Trump administration, which has been pushing for AI development in the U.S., but not a surprising result, as one database has shown that “America hates data centers,” with polls showing that 70% of Americans oppose AI data center build-outs.👨‍💻 THREAD on how data center-related ballot measures are faring tonight data centers are on the ballot in ~40 localities across 13 states, including proposed bans, votes on specific projects, and recalls of pro-data center politiciansNovember 4, 2026Note that the issues put to a vote are varied, ranging from outright permanent data center bans to moratoriums, time-limited actions, limitations based on size or consumption, and more. The mid-term elections also resulted in the recall of the mayor and two council members in Piqua, Ohio, and the mayor of Yukon, Oklahoma, for previously supporting data center bans. A second tracker of some 46 data center measures across 10 states reveals that of 33 measures to limit data centers, every single one is set to be passed. Of a further 13 positive measures to permit data centers and their construction, 11 look set to be defeated.Despite the overwhelming opposition to AI data centers, it’s unclear if they will affect projects that are already underway. In fact, out of the 300-plus local data center bans enacted across the U.S., only three developments totaling 2.3 gigawatts have been delayed, with 38 gigawatts expected to come online by 2027, and that investment into the infrastructure is still on track to hit $32 trillion by 2050. Nevertheless, these votes could affect future developments, especially as the U.S. Senate accuses Big Tech of misleading the public on the advantages of AI data centers. It’s also the reason why OpenAI and Anthropic are scrambling for small data center projects that range in capacity from 20 to 30 megawatts, especially as their hyperscale gigawatt sites face delays.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: President Donald Trump has taken steps to reduce the impact of data centers on the average citizen, like forcing AI data centers to pay an energy dividend to local communities and making tech companies, state governors, and utility companies promise to pay their own way via the “ratepayer protection pledge.” However, it seems that his effort was too little, too late, to change the minds of voters who are afraid of utility price hikes, noise pollution, and other negative effects that data centers have had on communities where they’ve been built. items.titleZh: 人工智能数据中心在美国中期选举中全面受挫——45项措施被列入选票，美国人以压倒性多数投票反对相关开发
items.descriptionZh:
美国多地围绕数据中心的地方公投在中期选举中呈现出压倒性的反对结果，成为特朗普政府推动美国AI发展的重大挫折。根据“Data Centers on the Ballot”追踪数据，在约40个地方辖区、13个州提出的数据中心相关措施中，已有33项限制数据中心开发的措施获胜，另有6项处于领先；只有北达科他州Harwood的一项措施失败，该措施要求对包括数据中心在内的工业项目增加额外审查程序，另有5项尚未公布结果。另一项覆盖10个州约46项数据中心措施的追踪显示，33项限制数据中心的措施全部有望通过；而在13项允许或支持数据中心建设的措施中，有11项预计将被否决。投票内容从永久禁止数据中心、暂停令、限期措施，到基于规模和能耗的限制不等。俄亥俄州Piqua市长和两名市议员、俄克拉荷马州Yukon市长也因与数据中心相关的先前立场被罢免。

这一结果并不令人意外。相关数据库显示“美国讨厌数据中心”，民调则显示70%的美国人反对AI数据中心建设。反对的主要动因包括公用事业费用上涨、噪音污染，以及数据中心已给当地社区带来的其他负面影响。文章指出，这并非单纯的反AI情绪，而是地方对数据中心实际负担的反弹。对于支撑大模型训练和推理的AI数据中心而言，其典型特征是高功耗、大规模和高电网需求：超大规模站点可达吉瓦级，需要长期电力保障、冷却系统和电网扩容，因而容易引发选址审批、社区同意和成本分摊争议。此次公投反映出的政策机制包括地方禁令、暂停令、规模与能耗限制、项目公投以及罢免支持相关项目的官员，显示出AI基础设施扩张正越来越受地方政治约束。

尽管反对声浪强烈，这些投票对已开工项目的影响仍不明确。全美已实施300多项地方数据中心禁令，但只有3个开发项目、合计2.3吉瓦被延迟；预计到2027年仍有38吉瓦数据中心上线，相关基础设施投资到2050年仍有望达到32万亿美元。不过，这些投票可能影响未来项目，尤其是在美国参议院指责大型科技公司误导公众、夸大AI数据中心优势的背景下。文章还提到，OpenAI和Anthropic正转向寻求容量20至30兆瓦的小型数据中心项目，部分原因是其吉瓦级超大规模站点面临延迟。

特朗普政府此前已采取措施减轻数据中心对普通民众的影响，例如要求AI数据中心向当地社区支付“能源红利”，并通过“费率payer保护承诺”让科技公司、州长和公用事业公司承诺自行承担相关成本。但文章认为，这些努力太少、太晚，未能改变担心电价上涨、噪音污染等问题的选民态度。整体来看，此次地方公投虽短期未显著阻挡已建和在建项目，但将提高未来AI数据中心在选址、审批、社区沟通和电力安排上的政治风险，可能促使企业调整项目规模、建设节奏和地方利益分配方式。

items.title: Nvidia can only fulfill 1% of China’s massive $70 billion GPU order for AI chips, report claims — supply constraints choke export-friendly RTX Pro 5500 deliveries despite huge demand
items.description: Just 1% of chips promised to major Chinese companies to power their AI ambitions will be delivered, according to reports.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Chinese technology giants ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent, among others, are set to receive only a limited number of Nvidia chips that they've ordered. Bloomberg is reporting that, according to unnamed sources, only "some tens of thousands, or roughly 1%" of RTX Pro 5500 workstation GPUs will be delivered over the next few months.Go deeper with TH Premium: GPUs (Image credit: Noctua)Desktop GPU RoadmapNvidia's Enterprise GPU RoadmapTesting DirectStorage with GPU decompressionThe GeForce RTX 30-series upgrade matrix — does your Ampere GPU need an upgrade in 2026?Rubin in-depthThe Stout Owl: The ultimate Noctua G2 PCDemand for the RTX Pro 5500 has far outstripped Nvidia's planned production. According to earlier reports, Chinese firms were suggested to have spent $35 billion on orders for over 3 million of the GPUs, far beyond Nvidia's ability to produce them. This new report suggests that amount has risen to $70 billion, at a cost of $11,000 per unit.Chinese demand for the RTX Pro 5500 is based on its performance and its unique status for shipping. The RTX Pro 5500 has the same CUDA cores as its flagship gaming GPU, the RTX 5090, but with a boosted 84GB GDDR7 memory count, so it's a good option for AI.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Unlike the RTX 5090, or other AI-focused workstation GPUs like the H200 and B300, there are no export limits, meaning it can be shipped to China without restrictions. China is in an arms race with the U.S. to produce better AI models, with GPUs like the RTX Pro 5500 being core to its success. Nvidia has reportedly halted RTX 5090 production to pivot towards its AI-focused enterprise base.The report suggests that Chinese developers expect a first batch of several thousand RTX Pro 5500 GPUs to be delivered by the end of 2026. In total, 700,000 RTX Pro 5500s are expected to be delivered by the end of 2027 as Nvidia increases its production, although this could change. items.titleZh: 报道称，英伟达仅能满足中国700亿美元AI芯片GPU巨额订单的1%——尽管需求巨大，供应限制仍阻碍面向出口的RTX Pro 5500交付
items.descriptionZh:
据Tom's Hardware援引彭博社报道，字节跳动、阿里巴巴、腾讯等中国科技巨头从英伟达订购的RTX Pro 5500工作站GPU将只能获得极为有限的交付量。匿名消息称，未来几个月内英伟达预计仅交付“数万颗、约占总订单1%”的RTX Pro 5500。这一缺口凸显中国AI算力需求与英伟达产能、出口合规产品供应之间的严重失衡。

背景方面，RTX Pro 5500已成为中国大型科技公司绕开美国高端AI芯片出口限制的重要选择。早前报道称，中国企业据称已花费350亿美元订购超过300万颗该GPU，远超英伟达原定产能；新报道则称订单金额已升至700亿美元，按每颗约1.1万美元计算，需求规模进一步膨胀。由于订单量远超供给，实际交付只能分批推进：中国开发者预计首批数千颗RTX Pro 5500将在2026年底前交付，到2027年底总交付量预计达到70万颗，但这一数字可能随英伟达增产计划调整。

从技术定位看，RTX Pro 5500并非H200、B300那类专用AI加速器，而是一款工作站GPU。其CUDA核心数量与英伟达旗舰游戏GPU RTX 5090相同，但显存提升至84GB GDDR7。对大模型而言，显存容量直接决定可承载的模型规模、推理并发能力和微调效率，因此84GB显存使其成为AI开发与部署中较有吸引力的选择。更关键的是，与RTX 5090以及H200、B300等产品不同，RTX Pro 5500没有出口限制，可以不受限制地运往中国。这使其在性能、CUDA生态兼容性和合规出货之间形成了独特组合，也是中国客户集中抢购的核心原因。

这一供应局面的影响在于，中国AI公司正与美国展开模型能力竞赛，GPU是训练和推理基础设施的核心。若RTX Pro 5500交付仅达订单的约1%，短期内中国科技巨头可获得的合规高端算力将明显受限，可能迫使其更依赖存量GPU、云算力租赁或国产替代方案，并影响大模型迭代节奏。与此同时，报道指出英伟达已停止RTX 5090生产，将产能转向AI导向的企业级产品，说明其正在把制造资源集中于需求更强、利润更高的AI计算市场。但即便增产，RTX Pro 5500的交付仍难以满足中国客户已达数百万颗级别的订单需求。

英伟达方面未对具体出货数字置评，但发言人在给彭博社的声明中批评美国出口管制，称“过时的美国出口管制覆盖了近五年前发布的游戏产品”，并称这些管制以及“中国自己对美国进口的限制”继续对公司形成约束。整体来看，RTX Pro 5500的交付短缺不仅是一次产品供不应求，更反映出AI算力竞争、出口管制与全球GPU产能分配之间的结构性矛盾。

history.content: With smartphone sales tanking by around 20 percent compared to 2025, Qualcomm is looking to data centers to help boost its bottom line. During its Q4 2026 earnings call, the company laid out its plans to make a splash in the AI data center business, through partnerships with companies like Amazon and Meta announced earlier this year. The company expects that portion of its business to grow quickly, forecasting around $650 million in data center revenue during the first quarter of 2027. But it anticipates that will reach $5 billion by the end of 2027 and $15 billion by 2029.Considering the company’s total revenue for 2026 was $10.4 billion, that would constitute a significant share of its earnings. It confirmed during the call that it expects data centers to eventually account for around 30 percent of its business.That’s not quite as ambitious as AMD, which says that it expects over 80 percent of its revenue will eventually come from data centers. history.titleZh: 智能手机销量下滑，高通大举押注数据中心
history.descriptionZh:
高通在2026财年第四季度财报电话会上明确表示，面对智能手机销售较2025年下滑约20%的压力，公司将把AI数据中心作为新的增长引擎。公司此前已宣布与亚马逊、Meta等超大规模云厂商合作，计划借此切入AI数据中心市场。高通预计，2027年第一季度数据中心业务收入约为6.5亿美元，到2027年底达到50亿美元，到2029年进一步增至150亿美元。作为参照，公司2026年总营收为104亿美元，因此数据中心业务若达到上述目标，将显著改变其收入结构。高通还确认，预计数据中心最终将占公司业务的约30%。

从技术层面看，这篇报道并未披露高通数据中心芯片的具体微架构、制程、内存带宽、互联规格或加速器型号，因此无法展开具体性能参数。可确认的是，其切入方式更偏向与亚马逊、Meta等云厂商合作，面向AI训练和推理所需的高能效计算与定制化加速需求。AI数据中心的核心技术挑战包括高算力密度、能效比、内存与互连带宽、规模化部署和软件生态；高通若能把其在低功耗计算和连接领域的积累延伸到数据中心场景，并通过定制合作锁定超大规模客户需求，将构成其业务创新的关键。但具体产品竞争力和技术细节仍有待后续披露。

从收入预测看，高通的数据中心业务呈现“低基数、高增速”特征：2027年第一季度约6.5亿美元，到2027年底50亿美元，意味着一年内大幅扩张；到2029年150亿美元，约为2027年第一季度规模的23倍。若以2026年104亿美元总营收为参照，150亿美元已超过该年总营收，因此30%占比目标隐含公司总营收同步增长或数据中心收入预测非常激进。与AMD预计未来80%以上收入来自数据中心相比，高通的30%目标相对温和，但也说明AI数据中心需求足够大、市场资金充足，竞争者仍有空间。

技术影响和应用场景方面，高通此举旨在降低对智能手机周期的依赖，形成第二增长曲线。AI数据中心业务可服务于大模型训练与推理、生成式AI服务、推荐系统、云计算和企业AI工作负载，并与亚马逊、Meta等云厂商的定制需求结合。若合作顺利落地，高通将从移动芯片供应商转向“移动+数据中心”双轮驱动；但执行风险包括合作规模能否兑现、产品能否在英伟达和AMD主导的数据中心加速市场中形成差异化，以及客户集中度和收入预测的可实现性。总体看，这是高通在手机业务承压下向AI基础设施转型的重要信号，但具体技术成色仍需产品与订单验证。

history.content: One of the basic problems of spending too much time on social media is that you are cooking your brain by reading posts from a pack of attention-seeking lunatics. If your social media of choice is the site formerly known as Twitter, and it is your main source of contact with the outside world, you may delusionally throw away nearly $500 million dollars on midterm elections, just like Elon Musk.In particular, $47 million of that money from Musk’s America PAC was aimed at defeating Texas Democrat James Talarico, who trounced Musk’s preferred Senate candidate, Ken Paxton, with 55 percent of the vote. Talarico even made Musk’s influence a central part of his campaign ads, with the slogan “Texas is not for sale.”The opposition to data centers is a way of making concrete how pissed off most people are with the tech industryHow did Musk get this so wrong? I blame the bubble of X. My former colleague Casey Newton, who has (with some well-earned shame) slunk back to X, explained that he did so because it was the site that was most influential with the AI crowd. In some sense, this is exactly the problem. The agentmaxxing loons of AI influencing are wildly out of touch with normal people. There is, right now, one very important bipartisan position in the United States, and it is: Fuck a data center.It’s pretty obvious that the opposition to data centers is a way of making concrete how pissed off most people are with the tech industry, particularly with the gangster tech regulation of late and the constant stream of threats coming from AI companies. These guys have really tied themselves and their AI aspirations to Donald Trump’s sinking ship, and if you’re hanging out on X all the time, that’s impossible to see, not least because the site’s owner, Musk, is shaping the algorithm in ways that make him feel good.Since Musk seems to have forgotten what it is like to experience joy, or even mild satisfaction, I have taken the liberty to make a list of things he could have bought to get him a better return on his investment. He probably could flip several things on this list for more money, but at minimum he could have gotten a little rush of pleasure from a new purchase:Larry Ellison’s private island ($300 million in 2012, $440 million in today’s dollars per CPI calculator) (source)13 Rolls-Royce La Rose Noire Droptails ($32 million) (source)5 The Graff Diamonds Hallucination watches ($55 million, $78 million today) (source)The Washington Post ($250 million in 2013, $360 million today) (source)30 Sunseeker 100 yachts (base price $14.6 million) (source)43 Hope diamonds ($300,000 in 1911, about $10.3 million today) (source)Ken Griffin’s NYC penthouse ($239.96 million in 2019, $321 million today) (source)76 New Zealand golden visas ($10 million plus $27,000 application fee in NZD, about $5.77 million in USD) (source)44 30-second Super Bowl commercials ($10 million) (source)At least 977 rides on Blue Origin’s New Shepard ($450,000) (source)Willem de Kooning’s Interchange (~$300 million, ~$400 million today) (source)$14.67 gift card to every Texan (~30 million Texans) (source)34 renovations of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool ($13.1 million) (source)223,000 Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards (at MSRP of $1,999) (source); 60,000 Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 graphics cards (at “globalized normal price” of $7,240) (source)8 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show Fantasy Bras (source)His very own non-Grok version of The Odyssey (budget $250 million) (source)4 sets of Wachtell, Lipton lawyers from the Twitter takeover suit ($90 million fee) (source)But hey, at least changing the name of SpaceX’s “Superintelligence” division back to “Artificial Intelligence” is free!Musk spent last night deleting tweets so he wouldn’t look as stupid as he is. Too bad it’s not as easy to delete other things! Texans were already asking questions about sweetheart deals to benefit Musk, and now there’s a wave of politicians who ran against his money coming into power, including the governor and the attorney general of Texas. That may mean unredacting Gov. Greg Abbott’s Musk emails, for instance — answering some questions about the influence Musk bought with Texas Republicans.So actually, maybe the best investment on that list would be the dream team of lawyers who clobbered Musk on the Twitter deal — because Musk has a bunch of new enemies in power, and the simplest thing in the world they can do to curry favor with their voters is investigate him. Bet you’d never know that if you spent all your time on X.

history.titleZh: 埃隆·马斯克本可浪费4.46亿美元的17个更好办法
history.descriptionZh:
埃隆·马斯克在中期选举中投入近5亿美元政治资金，试图影响多场选战，但结果令人失望。其中4700万美元通过其美国政治行动委员会用于阻击得克萨斯州民主党人詹姆斯·塔拉里科，然而塔拉里科以55%的得票率击败了马斯克支持的参议院候选人肯·帕克斯顿，甚至在竞选广告中以“得州非卖品”为口号，将马斯克的影响力作为核心议题加以抨击。

文章认为，马斯克此次政治判断失误的根源在于沉迷于X平台所营造的信息回音室。作者引述前同事凯西·牛顿的观察指出，X在人工智能从业者群体中最具影响力，而AI圈中热衷于“智能体最大化”的狂热者与普通民众严重脱节。当前美国存在一个罕见的跨党派共识：对数据中心说“不”。这种反对本质上是公众对科技行业不满情绪的具体化表达，尤其是针对近期科技监管中的强势作风以及AI公司不断发出的威胁性言论。文章指出，科技从业者已将自身AI抱负与特朗普的政治命运捆绑，但如果整日泡在X上，就完全看不到这一现实，因为平台所有者马斯克正通过算法塑造让自己感觉良好的信息环境。

为讽刺马斯克的投资回报，文章列举了他本可以用这笔钱购买的其他项目，包括甲骨文创始人拉里·埃里森曾拥有的私人岛屿、13辆劳斯莱斯定制车型、5块格拉夫钻石幻觉腕表、《华盛顿邮报》、30艘Sunseeker 100游艇、43颗希望钻石、肯·格里芬的纽约顶层公寓、76份新西兰黄金签证、44条30秒超级碗广告、至少977次蓝色起源新谢泼德号太空旅行、德库宁的画作《交换》、给每位得州人发放14.67美元礼品卡、34次林肯纪念堂倒影池翻修、22.3万张英伟达RTX 5090显卡，或者4套曾用于推特收购诉讼的Wachtell律所律师团队。

文章最后指出，马斯克已开始删除推文以掩饰尴尬，但得州选民早已对有利于他的特殊交易提出质疑。随着包括州长和总检察长在内的多位曾与马斯克资金对抗的政治人物上台，马斯克用金钱在得州共和党人中换取的影响力可能面临调查，例如要求公开州长格雷格·阿博特与马斯克的往来邮件。文章讽刺道，或许清单上最值得的投资，恰恰是那支在推特收购案中击溃马斯克的律师团队，因为马斯克如今在权力层中树敌众多，而新上台的政客讨好选民最简单的方式，就是对他展开调查。

history.title: Nintendo ROM chip supplier Macronix quits to focus on chips for AI data centers, reports indicate
history.description: Macronix, one of Nintendo's ROM chip manufacturers, is shutting down the business to reallocate manufacturing for NOR and NAND flash chips that the AI industry demands.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 10 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The death of physical games could be getting closer as Macronix, one of Nintendo’s key ROM chip suppliers for Switch and Switch 2 game cartridges, is reportedly shutting down its ROM business to focus on manufacturing NOR and NAND flash chips to supply data centers, multiple reports claim. Storage is already becoming expensive, and Macronix’s move may force Nintendo to increase cartridge prices, produce more Game-Key cards, or lean more towards digital purchases.Go deeper with TH Premium: Memory (Image credit: SK Hynix)AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supplySamsung debuts three next-generation memory technologies for AI data centersThe future of DRAM: From DDR5 to future ICsHigh-bandwidth memory roadmapInside the history of DRAM price-fixing lawsuits"Nintendo's main memory chip maker is quitting the Switch business," MST Financial David Gibson reports on X. "Macronix, which makes the ROM chips in Switch 1 and Switch 2 game memory cards, is phasing out that business. There will be no new ROM products, and Q3 is the last quarter it reports ROM sales separately.1/4 Nintendo's main memory chip maker is quitting the Switch business Macronix, which makes the ROM chips in Switch 1 and Switch 2 game memory cards, is phasing out that business. There will be no new ROM products, and Q3 is the last quarter it reports ROM sales separately.November 4, 2026He notes that Macronix ROM sales in Q3 of this year dropped to 5%, compared to last year’s 26%. Furthermore, Gibson says that the NT$37.8 billion capital expenditure is allocated to NOR and NAND Flash, leaving none for ROM as the company shifts its manufacturing capacity to supply AI needs — Taipei Times corroborated the report, stating, "At the same time, Macronix is gradually phasing out of ROM production, Wu said. It also reports that Macronix’s capital expenditure is split into two phases, the NT$ 22 billion for expanding manufacturing capacity, followed by an additional NT$15.8 billion for NAND flash used in eMMCs and 3D NAND.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Gibson expects that Nintendo’s digital margins will grow through more Game-Key Cards or digital-only sales, but as Macronix isn’t the only source of ROM chips, “physical cards will likely carry on for some time.” Gibson further reports that digital margins have been slowly rising, with numbers fluctuating depending on the quarter due to major physical game launches.3/4 My view: Macronix isn't Nintendo's only game memory card maker, so physical cards will likely carry on for some time. But at the margin, digital will grow, through more Game-Key Cards (which hold a download key, not the game) and digital-only sales.November 4, 2026ROHM group companies ROHM Semiconductor and LAPIS Semiconductor still supply ROM chips to Nintendo, so it’s unlikely that Nintendo will eventually go digital-only in the near future like Sony and Microsoft’s recent plans. With one less supplier, however, Nintendo may be forced to increase prices on physical games. You may like Nintendo stands by physical games as Sony embraces a digital-only future NOR Flash and SLC NAND production are under threat as capacity gets routed to more profitable products — 'severe undersupply' threatens everyday electronics Micron discontinues 2GB GDDR7 chips for gaming GPUs as it pivots toward higher-density memory for AI The biggest loser in all of this (besides the gamers), however, may be fabless chip design company MegaChips. Nintendo doesn’t buy ROM chips from Macronix directly; MegaChips designs the ROM chips according to Nintendo’s needs and, having no manufacturing capacity, outsources it to Macronix. MegaChips’ 2022 company report states that Nintendo accounted for 87.8% of its sales, while Macronix accounted for 67.8% of its outsourced manufacturing purchases. The report even states that if Macronix could manufacture ROM chips, “MegaChips’ operating results may be impacted.” The 2022 document further says that there was no sign that the risk would become apparent; however, the risk just became very real, and we’re not aware of MegaChips’ contingency plan to deal with this situation. However, Macronix and MegaChips have likely talked amongst themselves about Macronix’s plans to stop ROM chip manufacturing, and have given MegaChips some time to find another manufacturer before Macronix shuts down the ROM chip business. history.titleZh: 报道称，任天堂ROM芯片供应商旺宏退出，转而专注AI数据中心芯片
history.descriptionZh:
据报道，任天堂Switch和Switch 2游戏卡带的关键ROM芯片供应商之一旺宏电子（Macronix）正在逐步退出ROM业务，将制造重心转向NOR和NAND闪存，以供应快速扩张的AI数据中心。这一变化并非芯片技术本身的突破，而是存储产业产能重新配置的结果：AI数据中心对内存和存储的需求正在吞噬全球供应，使传统游戏卡带所需的ROM芯片在商业上变得不再优先。若消息属实，任天堂可能面临卡带成本上升、增加Game-Key卡（仅含下载密钥而非完整游戏）或进一步倾向数字销售的壓力，物理游戏的前景也因此再添不确定性。

从背景看，旺宏是任天堂Switch 1和Switch 2游戏存储卡中ROM芯片的主要制造商之一。MST Financial分析师David Gibson在社交平台X上指出，旺宏正在淘汰该业务，不会推出新的ROM产品，今年第三季度将是其最后一次单独报告ROM销售。数据显示，旺宏ROM销售占比已从去年的26%降至今年第三季度的5%。同时，该公司新台币378亿元资本支出全部投向NOR和NAND闪存，没有留给ROM；《台北时报》也印证了这一方向，称旺宏正逐步退出ROM生产。其资本支出分两阶段：先以新台币220亿元扩大制造产能，再追加新台币158亿元用于eMMC所需的NAND闪存和3D NAND。换言之，旺宏把有限产能从低增长、低利润的游戏卡带ROM转向AI数据中心所需的高价值存储产品。

这一供应链调整的影响需要从任天堂的卡带供应结构理解。任天堂并不直接向旺宏采购ROM芯片，而是由无晶圆厂芯片设计公司MegaChips根据任天堂需求设计ROM芯片，再外包给旺宏制造。MegaChips 2022年公司报告显示，任天堂占其销售额的87.8%，旺宏占其外包制造采购的67.8%；报告甚至警告，如果旺宏无法制造ROM芯片，“MegaChips的经营业绩可能受到影响”。当时这一风险尚未显现，如今却变得非常现实，而外界尚不清楚MegaChips有何应急预案。不过，旺宏与MegaChips很可能已就退出计划进行沟通，并给后者留出寻找替代制造商的时间。Gibson认为，由于旺宏并非任天堂唯一的游戏存储卡制造商，ROHM Semiconductor和LAPIS Semiconductor仍在向任天堂供应ROM芯片，物理卡带“可能还会持续一段时间”；但在边际上，数字销售会通过更多Game-Key卡和纯数字销售继续增长，任天堂的数字利润率也有望缓慢上升，具体数字会因重大实体游戏发售而按季度波动。

从性能和产业对比看，ROM芯片本身通常用于固化游戏数据，成本敏感、容量和读写需求相对固定；NOR和NAND闪存则面向代码存储、嵌入式存储和大容量数据存储，尤其3D NAND和用于eMMC的NAND在数据中心、移动设备和嵌入式市场具有更高附加值和更大需求。旺宏将新台币378亿元资本支出全部转向NOR/NAND，意味着其ROM业务已不再是战略重点；ROM销售占比从26%降至5%也说明该业务规模正在快速萎缩。对任天堂而言，少一个关键供应商可能推高物理游戏价格，或迫使公司生产更多Game-Key卡、扩大数字发行。对MegaChips而言，风险更为集中：任天堂贡献其近九成销售额，而旺宏又承担其近七成外包制造采购，一旦替代代工安排不能及时落地，其经营将受到明显冲击。总体来看，这一事件是全球存储产能向AI数据中心倾斜的缩影，短期内物理游戏不会立即消失，但实体卡带的成本、供应稳定性和数字化的相对吸引力都将发生变化。

history.title: Data centers lost the midterms
history.description:
Data center developers are poised to face a more restrictive building environment after voters across the country voted in candidates who favor moratoriums and ballot measures that put more obstacles on their expansion, delivering a stinging blow to a central pillar of the AI industry.
Of voters polled by NBC News on Election Day, 76 percent said they opposed data centers in their communities. Dozens of local communities voted directly to restrict development through ballot measures. And upset winners like Texas Democratic Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa and Michigan's Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed support moratoriums on development.
 …
Read the full story at The Verge.
history.content: Data center developers are poised to face a more restrictive building environment after voters across the country voted in candidates who favor moratoriums and ballot measures that put more obstacles on their expansion, delivering a stinging blow to a central pillar of the AI industry.Of voters polled by NBC News on Election Day, 76 percent said they opposed data centers in their communities. Dozens of local communities voted directly to restrict development through ballot measures. And upset winners like Texas Democratic Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa and Michigan’s Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed support moratoriums on development.It’s hard to draw a direct line from data center backlash to the election of any of these candidates, and there were still some races where candidates who favored more limited restrictions on data centers prevailed. Republican Rep. Byron Donalds, who previously lauded development in Florida, was elected as governor, and Iowa’s Democratic Governor-elect Rob Sand opposed a moratorium that his challenger favored. But even these candidates were forced to engage on data center issues during their campaigns, and will be likely to face continued pressure to put at least some guardrails in place.Ballot measuresVoters were faced with questions about data centers directly in 45 local ballot measures nationwide. As of Wednesday morning, according to a site compiled by Redbud Consulting, the results of 33 of those will restrict data center development. The Town of Wells, Maine, favored a 180-day moratorium on large data centers, backdated to mid-June 2026. Several cities in Ohio voted to ban data centers over 25MW. The City of El Dorado, Kansas, voted to ban data centers with peak electrical load over 10MW for 10 years.Dozens of local communities voted directly to restrict developmentTexasDemocratic state Rep. Gina Hinojosa will take over the governor’s seat from Republican incumbent Greg Abbott, marking a major Democratic flip in a state with the second-highest number of planned data centers. Hinojosa supports a statewide moratorium on data center development, while Abbott took a more measured approach. He announced a new audit this summer on data centers that could slow new developments from connecting to the state energy grid, but has previously praised data center expansion in the state.In another major upset, Democratic State Rep. James Talarico flipped Texas blue in a landmark Senate victory against Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton. Both Talarico and Paxton wanted to remove some tax exemptions for data centers, and to make them responsible for their own energy infrastructure-related costs. But Talarico also put an emphasis on the facilities’ environmental impact and ensuring they shared their profits with the public, while Paxton’s message focused on keeping Chinese tech out of data centers.FloridaRepublican congressman Byron Donalds won the governor’s seat over Democratic former congressman David Jolly. Donalds opposed an outright ban of data centers, while Jolly said he’d bar hyperscalers for a year beginning on day one in office. In Congress, Donalds introduced the Protecting Ratepayers Act, which would make developers pay for their own energy and water needs. Donalds’ win was still closer than expected in a state that’s been a Republican stronghold in the Trump era. As of Wednesday morning, NBC News reported that Donalds had exactly 50 percent of the vote, with 99 percent of expected votes already counted, while Jolly had 48.7 percent, and the rest went to an Independent candidate.PennsylvaniaDemocratic incumbent Governor Josh Shapiro held onto his seat against Republican challenger and state Treasurer Stacy Garrity. Both Shapiro and Garrity toughened their stances against data centers as the race went on, despite previously touting their potential benefits to the state. Shapiro signed an executive order that barred nondisclosure agreements for data center developments and took proposals for AI data centers off the fast track. Garrity has said she supports a development pause of up to three years.OhioDemocrat Sherrod Brown won back his former Senate seat from Republican incumbent Jon Husted, whom Brown had labeled “the face of data centers.” The National Republican Senatorial Committee warned this summer in a leaked memo that if data centers were blamed for Husted’s potential loss, it would make them seem poisonous to future candidates. Husted earlier helped install data center tax breaks as lieutenant governor, though he more recently introduced the Ratepayer Protection Act in Congress to force large data centers to cover their infrastructure upgrade and energy costs. Brown hammered Husted on the issue throughout the campaign, and while he hasn’t gone as far as to call for a moratorium, he’s said that developers shouldn’t get tax breaks or get a go-ahead without local input.Republicans warned that if data centers were blamed for Husted’s potential loss, it would make them seem poisonous to future candidatesMichiganDemocrat and former public health official Abdul El-Sayed won the Senate race over Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers. El-Sayed was one of the earliest politicians to stake his position on data centers, and has called for a pause on new developments “until we can do it safely and with federal protections.” Rogers called for a one-year state moratorium this summer, but not a federal ban.As of Wednesday morning, NBC News had not yet called a House race between Democratic organizer William Lawrence and Republican incumbent Tom Barrett, but Lawrence held a lead with 92 percent of the vote in. Similar to El-Sayed, Lawrence stated his position on data centers early on, calling for a one-year federal moratorium on new developments during his primary campaign. Barrett introduced legislation this summer to bar nondisclosure agreements for data center developments and give locals more control.MaineDemocrat and former Maine State Senator Troy Jackson ousted Republican Sen. Susan Collins from her Senate seat. The state legislature passed what would have been the country’s first moratorium on data centers, had the governor not vetoed it. But polls show that opposition to data centers among Maine residents remained strong. Jackson supported a state moratorium on data centers, while Collins opposed such a measure but called for more local control and protection for energy ratepayers.WisconsinDemocratic Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley won the governor’s race over Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany. Neither Crowley nor Tiffany favored a moratorium on data centers, and have distanced themselves from previous support. Crowley won his primary over progressive primary opponent Francesca Hong, who supported a moratorium. Both Crowley and Tiffany said they wanted to end state tax subsidies for data centers though they’ve accused one another of flip-flopping their stances.NevadaDemocratic Attorney General Aaron Ford successfully flipped the governor’s seat from incumbent Republican Joe Lombardo, whom he’d branded “data center Joe.” Lombardo has previously made supportive comments about data centers, but more recently introduced an executive order making tax incentives contingent on data centers covering power costs and meeting certain environmental standards. Ford previously championed a 2015 data center tax-break bill, but said today’s data centers are different from those years ago, and now supports a pause on all tax breaks for new data centers.GeorgiaDemocrat and former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms won the Georgia governor’s seat over Republican healthcare executive Rick Jackson. Bottoms favored a moratorium on data centers to review environmental and cost effects, while Jackson preferred to leave decisions up to locals.ArizonaDemocratic Gov. Katie Hobbs fought off a challenge from Republican Rep. Andy Biggs. Both opposed a moratorium on data centers in favor of power and water use standards.Democratic Attorney General Kris Mayes held onto her seat over a challenge from Republican state legislator Warren Petersen. Mayes took a more hardline view than her Democratic peer, Hobbs, by endorsing a state moratorium on data center development. Petersen opposed a moratorium, and said data centers are necessary for technology residents use every day.IowaDemocratic state auditor Rob Sand won the governor’s seat over Republican businessman Zach Lahn. Sand did not support a data center moratorium, which Lahn did. But both agreed on ending tax breaks for the developments.South CarolinaDemocratic pediatrician Annie Andrews flipped South Carolina’s Senate seat blue in a race against Republican incumbent Darline Graham, who had taken over the seat after her brother Lindsey Graham died. Andrews supported a two-year data center moratorium, while Graham opposed a pause and got significant support from a super PAC allied with the data center industry.
